primitives.name: Perceptual Ambiguity Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: and at last perceive more and more distinctly that it is the perfume of roses—until after all he discovers a bouquet of violets.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'sensory input signal (dimensionless)', 'B': 'belief state (dimensionless)', 'T': 'temporal evolution operator (time units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Sensory signals are ambiguous without contextual prior; belief evolves via Bayesian update.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When prior expectation dominates sensory input, leading to perceptual misattribution.

layer2.mapping: Belief state B(t+1) = P(S|B(t)) × P(B(t)) / P(S), where S is sensory input and B is prior belief.
layer2.telemetry: Change in perceptual classification over time with fixed stimulus.

primitives.name: Imagination-Induced Sensory Bias
primitives.verbatim_quote: This seemed to get lodged in my imagination as a sort of standard of perception; for, several days after the furnace had been rectified, I perceived the 'same smell' again.
primitives.assumptions: Memory traces of prior sensory experience bias subsequent perception.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When memory-induced expectation overrides actual sensory input.

layer2.mapping: Perception = S + I(M) where I(M) is a function of stored sensory memory.
layer2.telemetry: Repetition of perceived sensation despite absence of original stimulus.

primitives.name: Sensory Confabulation Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then suddenly he recognizes the violet-smell, and wonders how he could possibly have hit upon the roses.—Just so it is with taste.
primitives.assumptions: Confabulation occurs when expectation and real input are misaligned.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E ≠ R, resulting in C ≠ R, causing perceptual error.

layer2.mapping: C = f(E, R) where f is a nonlinear function representing cognitive distortion.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective shift in perception from actual to expected sensory identity.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that perception is not a passive process but an active inference mechanism shaped by prior expectations. The perceptual ambiguity operator demonstrates how sensory inputs are interpreted through a lens of belief, evolving from one hypothesis to another. This aligns with Bayesian inference where prior beliefs modulate posterior probabilities. The imagination-induced sensory bias shows that once a perceptual standard is formed in memory, it acts as a persistent reference point, distorting future perceptions even in the absence of the original stimulus. This mirrors how cognitive biases can persist beyond their causal origins. The sensory confabulation duality reveals that perception can be fundamentally deceptive when expectations override reality, creating a dualistic tension between what is sensed and what is believed. These primitives form a triadic structure: sensory input (S), belief (B), and expectation (E), where each influences the others in a feedback loop. The failure mode arises when E dominates S, leading to misperception. This framework supports a unified model of perception as a probabilistic inference engine subject to both internal and external noise.
